ctx.x: No, I didn't get into that. Not until months later. Ethel Waters was my favorite and I didn't get into that until later on when I was getting with into the Bix Goldke He band, Vince and I used to sit and listen to her records. But then they were beginning to be used more. When I was coming up in those days, let's say 1920, all the black records were race records.

You had to buy them under the race label and so consequently in the music stores where you'd go in and go into a booth, they wouldn't give you -- you'd have to ask for them, and many cases they didn't have them. Because they were interested in selling "Margie" and things like that that they had a lot of, "Whispering" and "Avalon" and all those things.
